actions.t: Check state pension forecast & fill NI gaps (gov.uk/check-state-pension)
actions.d:
Your state pension (~£11,973/yr full rate) does the heavy lifting from age 67 — make sure you're on track for the full amount.

  • Get your forecast at gov.uk/check-state-pension — it shows exactly how many qualifying NI years you have (35 needed for the full new state pension).
  • If years are missing, voluntary Class 3 contributions cost roughly £900 per year purchased and add about £340/yr to your pension for life — typically paying for itself within 3 years of claiming.
  • Call the Future Pension Centre (0800 731 0175) before paying — not every gap year actually increases your pension.
  • You'll keep earning NI through June 2027 from your salary, so check the forecast as at your retirement date, not today.

actions.t: Make one-off pension contribution — before taking any taxable pension income (MPAA)
actions.d:
This is your single biggest tax win before retiring, and the order matters.

  • About £24,730 of your £75k salary is taxed at 40%. Contributions up to that get 40% relief — £100 in the pension costs you £60.
  • Via salary sacrifice you also save 2% employee NI (and your employer may pass on some of their 15% saving — ask).
  • The annual allowance is £60,000, and unused allowance from the last 3 tax years can be carried forward if you want to go bigger with the inheritance.
  • Critical sequencing: once you take any taxable income from a pension, the MPAA cuts your future contribution allowance to £10,000/yr. Contribute first, draw later.
  • 25% of everything in the pension comes back out tax-free.

The ISA allowance is use-it-or-lose-it each tax year (6 April – 5 April), and ISA withdrawals in retirement are completely tax-free.

  • £20,000 this tax year from your cash — a Stocks & Shares ISA holding a low-cost global or S&P 500 index fund matches your stated goal.
  • Compare platform fees: flat-fee providers tend to win once balances exceed ~£50k; percentage-fee platforms are fine below that.
  • If markets feel uncomfortable, you can hold the £20k as cash inside the ISA and invest gradually — the allowance is secured either way.
  • A flexible ISA lets you withdraw and replace money in the same tax year without losing allowance — useful in retirement.

A second £20,000 goes in once the new tax year opens on 6 April 2027 — two months before you retire.

  • That makes £40,000 sheltered before retirement, and you can keep adding £20k every year after from remaining cash ("Bed & ISA" from any taxable investments).
  • Moving taxable investments into the ISA uses your £3,000 CGT allowance each year — sell in stages if gains are large.
  • Set a recurring April reminder; the dashboard's plan assumes this happens every year while cash remains.

The largest single decision in the plan. A sensible order of operations:

  • 1. Buffer: ring-fence 1–2 years of spending (£30–50k) in easy-access savings / cash ISA.
  • 2. Pension: consider topping up further while you still have salary — relief is at 40% only until June 2027 (annual allowance + carry-forward permitting).
  • 3. ISA: £20k per year, every year.
  • 4. The rest: a taxable account (GIA) in low-cost index funds, harvesting the £3,000 CGT allowance annually, plus Premium Bonds (up to £50k, prizes tax-free) for cash you want accessible.
  • Drip-feeding a lump sum over 6–12 months reduces regret risk, though investing immediately wins more often than not historically.
  • Check whether any inheritance tax is the estate's liability (it usually is) — what you receive is normally yours free of further tax.

actions.t: Book session with a regulated independent financial adviser
actions.d:
With ~£400k+ and an irreversible set of decisions (MPAA, drawdown method, inheritance), one or two paid advice sessions are worth it.

  • Find advisers at unbiased.co.uk or vouchedfor.co.uk — look for "Chartered" or "Certified" financial planners who are independent (whole of market), and check the FCA register.
  • Ask up front: fixed fee vs % of assets. A one-off retirement plan typically runs £1,500–£3,500 fixed — avoid open-ended % fees if you mainly want a sense-check.
  • Bring this dashboard's CSV/JSON export — a concrete plan to critique gets you far more value per hour.
  • Also free: Pension Wise (MoneyHelper) offers a government-backed guidance appointment for over-50s — book it regardless.

Check the mechanics of getting money out before you need it.

  • Confirm your plan supports flexi-access drawdown and partial withdrawals (UFPLS-style), the annual fee on your plan, and how long withdrawals take to process.
  • Expect emergency tax on your first taxable withdrawal (HMRC applies a Month 1 code) — you reclaim it with form P55/P50Z, usually within 30 days. Plan cash flow around it.
  • Decide 25% tax-free as a lump vs taking it gradually with each withdrawal — gradual usually preserves more tax-free growth and is what this dashboard models.
  • Compare drawdown fees with one or two other SIPP providers; transfers before drawdown are straightforward.

actions.t: Ring-fence 1–2 years' spending as cash buffer
actions.d:
A cash buffer means you never sell investments in a downturn to pay for groceries.

  • Target £30,000–£50,000: roughly 1–2 years of your £2k/month core spending plus holiday money.
  • Spread across: easy-access savings for year one, a 1-year fixed-rate account for year two, and/or a cash ISA portion.
  • Mind FSCS protection — £85,000 per banking licence. With the inheritance landing, split across institutions.
  • Your CGT-free gold and silver coins (£30k) are a decent second-line reserve for lumpy expenses — they're in the plan as exactly that.
